flagged.evidence: The contract says: “The Definition applies when P or Q is empty: the empty function is then the unique order isomorphism.” For P = ∅ and Q = {q}, the empty function is not surjective, so it is not an order isomorphism. The empty case applies only when both carriers are empty.
The contract quotes “x <=_P y iff f(x) <=_Q y,” while the current Definition states “x <=_P y iff f(x) <=_Q f(y).” The contract omits f(y), so it does not accurately quote the defining condition.

The contract says “0 does not inject into the empty set.” Since 0 = ∅, the empty function is an injection 0 → ∅. The first ordinal that does not inject into ∅ is 1; the contract's H = {0} computation is consistent with this correction.

The contract says the Remarks “cite the dependent-choice page only to contrast well-founded descent with the failure of infinite descending sequences in general orders.” The current Remark instead says, “This direction follows directly from the definition; no converse is used here.” The body contains no such dependent-choice citation or comparison.

The contract calls “the case a in I” central. The current Remark defines a = min(W \ I), so a is outside I; the converse inclusion explicitly uses a ∉ I. The contract describes the proof with the opposite premise.

The contract says steps 3.1 and 5.1 treat W already an ordinal and that “no proper initial segment is involved.” Step 3.1 proves general order reflection; step 5.1 explicitly invokes a proper initial segment to prove uniqueness. These locations do not establish the ordinal-input identity case.

The contract locates least-element applications in steps 1.1 and 2.1, which prove order algebra and induction. The current proof applies the well-ordering fact in steps 3.1 and 3.2, including the statement that “every nonempty subset of n has an ∈-least element by [L5].”

The contract says steps 1.1 and 1.2 locate the cost of obtaining the class function. Those steps establish transfinite induction and recursion in ZF. The current discussion of the cost of “obtaining that class function” is in step 3.1.
